key_insight: For low-Prandtl-number liquid-metal heat transfer, the simplest closure—k-ω SST with Kays’ turbulent Prandtl correlation—was the most robust and consistently accurate, outperforming more complex thermal turbulence models.
engineering_relevance: For CFD of liquid-metal cooling systems, model choice strongly affects thermal predictions, and this study identifies which RANS closures are dependable enough for engineering use.
method: Assessed multiple RANS thermal closures in OpenFOAM v2212: k-ω SST + Kays Pr_t, four-equation k-ε-kθ-εθ, logarithmic k-Ω-kθ-Ωθ, and algebraic heat-flux models.
Validated models on channel flow, pipe flow, and heated backward-facing step cases against DNS and prior published results.
Compared reproducibility, numerical robustness, and temperature-field accuracy across the closures.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark flows, the k-ω SST + Kays model performed best overall, the k-ε-kθ-εθ model was the most consistent multi-equation alternative, and some published formulations could not be reproduced reliably.
watch_item: Several higher-order closures showed robustness issues or failed to reproduce thermal results, so implementation details and model-form consistency are critical.
paper_title: Critical assessment of RANS Models for Turbulent Heat Transfer in Low-Prandtl-Number Forced Convection
